Subject: Post-demo: Embedding / Rerank bench plan & hyperscaler comparison

Thanks for your time today, Sam — great conversation. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Goal: give QuillDocs a defensible apples-to-apples for embeddings + rerank across Redwood Hosted, Redwood Dedicated (quantized), and two hyperscaler inference endpoints your infra team is evaluating. Primary metrics: retrieval latency (p50/p95), recall@k (k=1/5/10), end-to-end rerank latency, and unit cost (per-query and storage).

2) Proposed benchmark matrix (attached as QLD_MVP_eval_matrix.xlsx):
   - Corpus: 10k representative documents (you agreed to provide the sample subset; sample-queries-10k.jsonl attached)
   - Embedding dims: 512 and 1536 (compare recall vs cost)
   - Retrieval technique: ANN (FAISS HNSW) + dense vectors; rerank stage uses 1-pass cross-encoder or lightweight re-ranker depending on latency profile
   - Tests: cold-lookup latency, warmed cache latency, throughput (QPS sweep), recall@1/5/10, and index size/cost per month

3) Hyperscaler comparison notes we discussed: latency variability at scale (multi-tenant noisy neighbors), minimum billed token/compute slabs, and differences in vector quantization support. We will include a notes section in the summary PDF.

4) Owners & timeline:
   - QuillDocs: share 10k sample documents and 1k query set (Priya to confirm by EOD Monday)
   - Redwood: run bench across Hosted, Dedicated quantized, and a dedicated Dedicated-like config that mirrors your latency SLOs. Deliverables in 6 business days: raw metrics CSVs, short summary PDF (redwood-vs-hyperscalers-summary.pdf), and suggested config (batching/kv cache/quantization) to meet your target SLA.

5) Pricing ask: Priya — you mentioned needing a delta for 512 vs 1536 dims including storage. We'll provide a TCO table in the summary.

Attachments: QLD_MVP_eval_matrix.xlsx, sample-queries-10k.jsonl

If that aligns, I'll kick off the bench and loop Marissa for technical details. Happy to schedule a 30-min sync next week to review the results.

Thanks,

Thanks Rishi — adding a few technical clarifications that will affect measurements and costs: 

- Embedding dims: 512 uses smaller index memory and typically 2-3x faster ANN lookup vs 1536, but recall often drops ~5-12% depending on corpus. We'll report recall@1/5/10 and also include an interpolation curve.
- Quantization: for Dedicated we recommend 4-bit Q4_0 for 1536-d to reduce memory while retaining >95% recall for rerank candidates; we'll test both FP16 (baseline) and Q4_0.
- KV/prefix caching: if you have repeated query prefixes (search-as-you-type), caching will dramatically reduce p50 but p95 still depends on hot keys — please flag if you expect lots of autocomplete traffic.
- Rerank: We'll run two configurations: (A) dense retrieval + lightweight bi-encoder reranker (fast, lower cost) and (B) cross-encoder rerank (higher latency, higher quality) for a subset of 1k queries to measure quality vs latency tradeoff.

Data we need from QuillDocs: 
- 10k documents (text or HTML cleaned) + 1k labeled queries if you have them (preferred) -- otherwise we'll use the 1k query sample you have.
- Target SLOs (p95 < 200ms for retrieval? or p95 < 400ms acceptable?) so we can tune batching and routing.

I'll instrument the bench to output: median/95th latency, recall curves, index size (GB), and estimated monthly storage & per-query compute cost.

Marissa

Thanks — this looks great. A few clarifying Qs from Product/Finance perspective before we hand-off sample data: 

1) For storage and TCO, can you provide an example line-item showing monthly cost for 10k docs at 512 vs 1536 dims (index size + storage + baseline inference cost) — ballpark numbers are fine.
2) For latency SLOs: our users expect search results in ~300ms globally; is that p95 retrieval only or end-to-end? If p95 retrieval is 200ms but cross-encoder rerank pushes end-to-end to 450ms, we need guidance on tradeoffs.
3) On the hyperscaler comparison: can Redwood include one managed hyperscaler vector endpoint (their managed embedding API) and one self-hosted FAISS on a GCP VM? We want both managed and self-hosted comparisons.

We can share the 10k sample by Monday. Also attaching a short doc with our expected query mix (search-heavy, some autocomplete) — will upload to the Drive link after this email.
